title: Colorado's 3rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Colorado's 3rd Congressional District encompasses the Western Slope, including Grand Junction, Pueblo, and Montrose. Incumbent Republican Rep. Jeff Hurd, first elected in 2024 with 50.8% of the vote, is seeking a second term in a district that leans Republican (Cook PVI: R+5) and has not elected a Democrat since 2011. Hurd faces a primary challenge from former state Rep. Ron Hanks, while Democrats Alex Kelloff and Dwayne Romero compete in their own primary. The general election is rated 'Likely Republican' by Cook Political Report, though Democrats see an opportunity in presidential-year turnout and backlash to Trump administration policies. Heather Barton is also running as an unaffiliated candidate.
polling_note: Two polls have been conducted for a potential Hurd vs. Kelloff general election matchup. No polls including Dwayne Romero, Ron Hanks, or Heather Barton were found.

candidates.name: Jeff Hurd
candidates.summary: Jeff Hurd is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A Colorado native and attorney, Hurd is a member of the moderate Republican Governance Group and has served on the House Committees on Natural Resources, Science, Space and Technology, and Transportation and Infrastructure. He is running for re-election and has been endorsed by President Donald Trump after a brief rescission and reinstatement of that endorsement.

candidates.name: Ron Hanks
candidates.summary: Ron Hanks is a former Colorado State Representative (2021-2023) and a retired U.S. Air Force veteran of 32 years. He ran for U.S. Senate in 2022 and previously challenged for this House seat in 2024, losing the primary to Jeff Hurd. Hanks participated in the January 6, 2021 Capitol protest and has promoted claims of election fraud. He is running on a conservative platform emphasizing immigration enforcement, opposing mail-in voting, and supporting Trump administration policies.

candidates.name: Alex Kelloff
candidates.summary: Alex Kelloff is a businessman and entrepreneur who co-founded Armada Skis, with family roots in Colorado's 3rd District dating back to 1893. He has a 30-year career in finance and telecommunications, including serving as a partner at SDC Capital Partners and as Head of Telecommunications Investment Banking at Jefferies. Kelloff holds a BBA from James Madison University, an MS from Johns Hopkins University, and an MBA from INSEAD, and is running on a platform of healthcare access, public lands protection, and economic opportunity.

candidates.name: Dwayne Romero
candidates.summary: Dwayne Romero is a U.S. Army veteran, former Army Ranger, and Bronze Star recipient who served as a Combat Engineer Executive Officer during the Persian Gulf War. He has served on the Aspen City Council, Aspen School District Board of Education (including as President), and various local boards. Romero also served as Director of Economic Development under Gov. John Hickenlooper and owns a property management company on the Western Slope. He is running on a platform of reversing healthcare cuts, protecting public lands, and restoring federal funding for Colorado communities.

candidates.name: Heather Barton
candidates.summary: Heather Barton is an unaffiliated candidate running for U.S. House representing Colorado's 3rd Congressional District. She declared her candidacy for the general election and has filed paperwork with the Federal Election Commission. Limited public information is available about her background and policy positions beyond her campaign statement that she is 'fighting for the working class, not the ruling class.'

forecast.rationale: Colorado's 3rd District leans Republican (Cook PVI: R+5) and has not elected a Democrat since 2011. Incumbent Jeff Hurd, elected in 2024 with 50.8%, is seeking a second term. Two available general-election polls (both partisan-affiliated) test a Hurd-Kelloff matchup, showing Hurd ahead by 5 and 9 points, averaging a ~7-point lead. Cook Political Report rates the race 'Likely Republican.' Uncertainty is medium due to: only two polls from partisan firms, unsettled Democratic primary (Kelloff vs. Romero), a Republican primary challenge from Ron Hanks, and an unaffiliated candidate (Heather Barton) who could shift vote shares. Presidential-year turnout and potential backlash to Trump policies add further uncertainty. Nonetheless, incumbency, district partisanship, and the limited polling all point to a clear Republican advantage consistent with the 'likely R' rating (~85% win probability) and an estimated margin around 6 points.
